messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: rstan install fails
parts:
Stan's compiler doesn't build *under Windows* without optimization.
The problem with -O0 is that the debug info being generated blows
out the memory of their rather lame C++ toolchain. We've had to
implement several painful workarounds even to get the optimized
versions to compile under Windows.

None of the dev team uses Windows for development, so we use it
for our integration server just to make sure it's getting tested.
We're going to add continuous integration for Linux and Mac OS soon,
though it's never caused us a problem --- basically if something
can be made to work on Windows, it has worked everywhere else.

Everyone uses different debugging tactics. I'm still a fan of
debug-by-printf. I almost always find it easier than using
a step-through debugger. I do find debuggers really useful to
get a feel for the call chain in code I'm not familiar with.
I believe others use gdb, Xcode, and various memory profiling
tools for leaks. I think most of our profiling has been in Xcode,
though that's just because I don't know what the linux users use.

- Bob

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: rstan install fails
parts:
rstan cannot be built with O0 using g++ (see here https://travis-ci.org/stan-dev/rstan/builds/31240900, where rstan was built with combinations of clang/gcc and optimization O0 and O3).  This is a different issue than we can only build stan with O0 on windows.  This is a problem for rstan for quite some time, maybe since we have rstan.  One difference for rstan (essentially stanc) is that we are building a shared library, but we are building an executable in stan.  But I cannot really figure out what is the underlying problem.  

Jiqiang
